label: prop:markov-trace-hecke-functional
title: The Markov trace is a linear functional on $H_n(q)$, and the connected-sum rule
html:
Let R be a commutative ring and z, h \in R. Let H_\infty be the Hecke tower over R: generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \ldots with \sigma_m^2 = h\,\sigma_m + 1, the braid relations and far commutation. Write H_m \subset H_\infty for the subalgebra generated by \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{m-1}, and y^{\uparrow k} for y with every generator index raised by k. There is an R-linear map \mathrm{tr}_M : H_\infty \to R that agrees with the word trace of the recursive reducer on every positive word. It satisfies:

  1. \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) = \mathrm{tr}_M(yx);

  2. \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_m) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_m;

  3. \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,y^{\uparrow m}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m and any y; in particular \mathrm{tr}_M(y^{\uparrow m}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(y), and \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m;

  4. (connected-sum rule) \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_m\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y) for x \in H_m and any y;

  5. for an interface letter a + b\,\sigma_m with a, b \in R,

    \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,(a + b\,\sigma_m)\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = (a + b z)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y).

Let q, s \in R with s^2 = q and s h = q - 1. Then \sigma_i \mapsto s\,\sigma_i is an algebra map from H_n(q), presented with \sigma_i^2 = (q-1)\sigma_i + q, into H_\infty. Composing gives a linear trace on H_n(q) with \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = s z. When R is a field and q \neq 0, for every splitting of H_n(q) into matrix blocks this trace equals x \mapsto \tau(x\,\kappa) for a central element \kappa, where \tau is the canonical symmetrizing trace.

Proof

The word trace satisfies the Hecke, braid and far-commutation relations inside any two-sided context of words. Extended linearly to the free algebra, it therefore vanishes on the two-sided ideal of the defining relations and descends to H_\infty. Cyclicity passes from words to the algebra by linearity. Every element of H_m is a linear combination of words in \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{m-1}, so the Markov property and the shared-strand product law of the reducer extend linearly to (2) and (3). Shift invariance is (3) with x = 1; the split form is (3) for x \in H_m \subset H_{m+1}. Then (4) is (3) applied to x\,\sigma_m \in H_{m+1}, followed by (2). For (5), expand the interface letter and apply (3) and (4).

For H_n(q), (s\sigma)^2 = q(h\sigma + 1) = (q-1)(s\sigma) + q, because q h = s(sh) = s(q-1). The braid and far-commutation relations are homogeneous, so the rescaling respects them. The knot-factor statement is the general fact that every cyclic trace on H_n(q), for q \neq 0 and a splitting into matrix blocks, equals x \mapsto \tau(x\,\kappa) for a unique central \kappa; it is applied here to the trace just constructed.

Remark on scope

Rule (5) shows that a bond made of one crossing contributes the same factor a + b z whichever two clusters it joins. On the finite algebras, the inclusion H_m(q) \to H_n(q) (\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i) and the shift H_p(q) \to H_n(q) (\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_{i+k}) commute with the rescaling into the tower. So the trace on H_n(q) restricts to the trace on H_m(q), and for m + 1 + p \leq n,

  \mathrm{tr}_n\bigl(x\,\sigma_m\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = s z\,\mathrm{tr}_m(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_p(y), \qquad x \in H_m(q),\ y \in H_p(q).

The factor s comes from the rescaling \sigma_m \mapsto s\,\sigma_m.

Remark on normalisation

The parameter q of H_n(q) here is the one of the relation \sigma_i^2 = (q-1)\sigma_i + q, with eigenvalues q and -1. The generator \sigma_i of H_n(q) maps to s times the tower generator \sigma_i, and the tower generators satisfy (\sigma_i - Q)(\sigma_i + Q^{-1}) = 0 with Q = s, since h = s - s^{-1} when s is a unit. So the tower is the Hecke algebra in the normalisation with eigenvalues Q and -Q^{-1}, h = Q - Q^{-1} and Q^2 = q.

Remark on bond words

The same argument covers any bond word placed on its own block of generators. If x \in H_m, B \in H_k and y is arbitrary, then B^{\uparrow m} uses \sigma_m, \ldots, \sigma_{m+k-1} and shares one strand with each cluster, and

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,B^{\uparrow m}\,y^{\uparrow (m+k)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(B)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y).

For B = V^3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in H_2, a direct computation in H_3 with \sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_1 - h gives the factor \mathrm{tr}_M(V^3) = 1 - h^4 + h^4 z^2 - h^5 z, the Borromean trace.

The \gamma\gamma bond (\sigma_2\sigma_3^{-1})^3 = (V^3)^{\uparrow 2} between a first nucleon word x \in H_2 and a second nucleon word y^{\uparrow 3} is not of this block form: its letter \sigma_3 is also a generator of the second nucleon. For a bond B \in H_2 that overlaps the second cluster in this way,

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,B^{\uparrow m}\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(B\,y^{\uparrow 1}\bigr), \qquad x \in H_m,

and the same holds with the bond placed after y^{\uparrow (m+1)}. The bond ratio \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,B^{\uparrow m}\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) / \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(B\,y^{\uparrow 1}\bigr)/\mathrm{tr}_M(y), where defined, is therefore a function of the second cluster alone.

Remark on bonds that enter both clusters

Let x, A \in H_m and let Y, C be arbitrary. A bond A\,C^{\uparrow (m+1)} that uses generators of both clusters but not \sigma_m gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,Y^{\uparrow (m+1)}\,A\,C^{\uparrow (m+1)}\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(xA)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(YC).

With one interface letter a + b\,\sigma_m between two such pieces, the factor a + bz appears in front. In both cases the bond ratio of a pair (x, y) is a product f(x)\,g(y), so the four ratios satisfy \mu_{pp}\,\mu_{nn} = \mu_{pn}\,\mu_{np}. When all four are positive, \mu_{pn} < 1 and \mu_{np} < 1 together with \mu_{pp} > 1 and \mu_{nn} > 1 is impossible.

Remark on the bond chain

For a chain of clusters N_0, N_1, \ldots, N_k in which a bond V^3 is placed after each cluster and overlaps the next one,

  \mathrm{tr}_M = \mathrm{tr}_M(N_0)\,\prod_{j=1}^{k} \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(V^3\,N_j^{\uparrow 1}\bigr).

The difference between the trace of the chain without bonds and the trace with bonds is therefore a polynomial in the single-cluster quantities \mathrm{tr}_M(N_j) and \mathrm{tr}_M(V^3 N_j^{\uparrow 1}).

Remark on the knot factor and trace differences

For any trace t(x) = \tau(x\kappa) and any two elements a, c, linearity gives t(a) - t(c) = \tau\bigl((a - c)\,\kappa\bigr), so a difference of traces is the pairing of a difference of elements with one knot factor. On a split element x \cdot y^{\uparrow m} the pairing with the knot factor of H_n equals the product of the pairings with the knot factors of the two smaller algebras. The functional x \mapsto t(x\,b) is paired by b\kappa, and it is a trace exactly when b\kappa is central.

Remark on two interface letters

With two interface letters u = \alpha + \beta\sigma_m and v = \gamma + \delta\sigma_m, the trace of a bond between two clusters is a sum of products of single-cluster traces plus \beta\delta times one term in which two 2-cables cross, \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(P\,Q^{\uparrow}\,\sigma_{n+1}\sigma_n\sigma_{n+2}\sigma_{n+1}\bigr). That cable term does not split into a product. When one side of the bond carries no inner interface letter, the cable term is absent and the cross-ratio identity holds again.

Remark on two bonds into one cluster

Let a be any bond and N any cluster. The trace of a^{\uparrow 1}\,(\sigma_0\,a^{\uparrow 1}\,\sigma_0^{-1})\,N^{\uparrow 2} is unchanged when \sigma_0 is replaced by \sigma_0^{-1} in the transport, and when the two bonds are exchanged.

Remark on strand reflection

Let w be a positive word in \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}, and let w^{P} be the word obtained by replacing each \sigma_a with \sigma_{n-1-a}. Then \mathrm{tr}_M(w^{P}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(w). The half-twist \Delta_n satisfies \Delta_n \sigma_a = \sigma_{n-1-a} \Delta_n for a < n by the braid and far-commutation relations, and it is invertible, so w^{P} = \Delta_n w \Delta_n^{-1}, and cyclicity gives the equality. The Markov property is stated only at the top generator, but the trace still does not distinguish the two ends of the strand line.
